title: Hidden Giants: Artificial Nest Boxes as a Non‐Invasive Method for Estimating Density of a Declining Giant Salamander, the Eastern Hellbender (Cryptobranchus alleganiensis alleganiensis)
content:
ABSTRACT

The eastern hellbender salamander (Cryptobranchus alleganiensis alleganiensis) is a threatened amphibian that lives in clean freshwater streams in the Eastern United States. Understanding population trends is fundamental in making conservation and management decisions. However, collecting data to estimate population density and demographic parameters for hellbenders is difficult, and typically uses intensive rock-lifting surveys, which disturb the animals and their habitat. This is the first study to estimate hellbender population size using capture-recapture techniques that use minimally invasive data collection methods. We created and installed 150 artificial nest boxes in two waterways in western Pennsylvania. We built capture histories from 18 survey occasions between 2019 and 2021 at five reaches in one waterway (PA1) and three reaches in the other (PA2). We recorded a total of 290 captures of adult hellbenders, including 178 captures of 82 uniquely identified individuals and 112 captures of unmarked individuals. Using POPAN capture–recapture models, we found that adult hellbender density was lower in PA2 at 0.28 adults/100 m2 (95% CI = 0.19–0.37) than in PA1 at 0.61 adults/100 m2 (95% CI = 0.48–0.72). In addition, hellbender body sizes did not significantly differ between our study and a rock-lifting survey dataset collected during the study period at PA2, but animals captured during rock-lifting surveys were slightly smaller at PA1. Although nest boxes are not used by non-breeding, young animals, the similarity in animal size between nest box and rock-lifting surveys suggest that nest boxes can be used successfully to evaluate trends in eastern hellbender adult population. We recommend artificial nest boxes as an effective tool for non-invasive population monitoring in other parts of the hellbender's range to produce robust and comparable population estimates and detect numeric trends.
